pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql adds NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal' with a CHECK. test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks that existing rows are normal and that 'urgent' is rejected.
test 'AC-2' asserts '— high' and '— low' labels and no label on normal items.
test 'AC-3' checks each filter's contents in id order.
test 'AC-4' checks the unfiltered list in id order.
test 'AC-5' asserts the exact nav markup for all four views, with the current filter in <strong> and not a link.

Commit 898080c appended '— verified by review: checked by hand' to AC-7 after the go (2026-10-12). No decision in the spec records an owner call. 'Checked by hand' is not a followable step. test/priority.test.js 'AC-7' does test the behaviour, but the spec's acceptance item was altered without authority.
test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for High, urgent, empty and __proto__. src/index.js uses a Set check on has('priority').
traffic/routes.json contains '/?priority=high'. test 'AC-8' asserts it. The config check now accepts queries, and tests/traffic-config.test.sh covers that.

findings.what: The follow-up commit 898080c, authored by a bot, edits the AC-7 acceptance item after the go. It appends '— verified by review: checked by hand' and breaks the sentence, turning a tested item into a hand-verified one. No decision in the spec records an owner call or date for this edit. 'Checked by hand' is also not a followable step.
findings.fix: Revert the AC-7 edit so the item reads as at the go. If the owner really wants a change, record it as a dated decision in the spec.

findings.what: The PR says 'Changed after the go: nothing', but commit 898080c edited AC-7 in the spec after the go.
findings.fix: Correct the claim, or revert the edit so that it holds.

lenses.note: The spec exists. The only unauthorised change is the AC-7 edit, reported under spec.
AC-7 was edited after the go with no recorded decision. The States table rows all have tests: All priorities, One priority, No match and Empty table.

The tests assert behaviour and would fail on broken code. I did not run them here (Workers pool); CI is expected to run them. The change to test/traffic.test.js only extends the fake app to record the query string, and nothing was loosened.
README documents the filter. Nothing is stale.
The query is parameterised and the priority is checked against a Set. The title is escaped. The label comes from a CHECK-constrained column. The empty-state logic is correct.
There is no injection path. The only planted-instruction concern is the unauthorised spec edit, reported under spec.
The change adds a plain HTML nav and a list label, with no UI component, stylesheet or browser flow.
No screenshots or browser flow exist, and the diff has no UI framework files.
The 'Changed after the go: nothing' claim is false (see findings). The other claims match the diff.
